For anything beyond a low garden edge, yes. A professional understands footings, drainage, batter and the WA permit and engineering requirements, and stands behind the finished wall. What is the price per metre for a retaining wall in WA? Price per square metre of wall face is the standard way Perth quotes are compared. Expect roughly $250-$600/m2 for limestone block and $450-$700/m2 for concrete post and panel, before excavation, drainage and engineering are added. Do retaining walls over 500mm need a permit in Perth? Generally yes. 500 mm (0.5 m) of retained ground is the state exemption threshold under Building Regulations 2012 Schedule 4 - above it, a building permit is required. Do I need a building permit for a retaining wall in WA? In Western Australia, Building Regulations 2012 Schedule 4 exempts a retaining wall from a building permit only if it retains no more than 0.5 m of ground, is not tied to any other building work or the protection of adjoining land, and does not affect a boundary wall or dividing fence. Always confirm with your local government before work starts. How do you know if a retaining wall is failing? Common warning signs are a visible lean or bulge in the wall face, horizontal cracking, gaps opening at the base, water pooling or seeping through the face after rain, and soil settling or slumping above the wall.
